It's in many ways a mutual feeling. The big reason that it's LGBT is because that's basically who was at the Stonewall Riots. While a lot of trans people are LGB, there really isn't much connecting the two groups. There's still a lot of people confused on the differences, and it also forces the movement to split its time.

While the goals of the two groups is "acceptance" it isn't really acceptance of the same things. There is some overlap between the two groups in that many trans people are gay, but overall, what they are trying to get society to accept and treat equally has very little to do with gay rights.

It's similar to the labor rights movement in the 1800s and early 1900s. The labor movement had fairly clear and concise goals in that it wanted rights and bargaining power for laborers. Then, someone noticed that many civil rights groups had overlapping goals. It made some sense to team up for political expediency, but overall it intertwined two groups that had very little to do with each other. In the end, the labor rights movement kept getting and is still getting dragged into fights that weren't theirs and had/has very little to do with their goals.
